summary: P99 tail-latency and request timeouts caused by GPU headroom exhaustion + autoscale sizing mismatch in dedicated reservation
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC SparkWrite observed elevated p99 latency and intermittent 504/timeout errors on their dedicated GPU reservation. Impact: customer reports degraded inference throughput for production chat endpoint resulting in user-facing timeouts and increased error budget usage. Environment: prod - dedicated reservation (pool id: pool-us-east-09), region us-east-1, serving runtime v2.18.1, autoscaler v1.7.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send sustained mixed-length chat traffic (seq len 512-2048) to customer's production route for 30+ minutes via their integration test harness.
2) Observe p95/p99 latency climb and eventual 504 responses for ~1-3% of requests during peaks.
3) Check cluster GPU utilization and request queue depth in the reservation.

Observed logs/metrics:
- p95 rose from ~240ms to ~780ms, p99 spiked to ~2.3s at peak windows.
- Error responses roughly 2.7% 504/timeout during 09:10-09:40 UTC window.
- GPU utilization on several nodes reached 98-100% sustained while some other nodes in the same reservation were idle (GPU headroom imbalance).
- Autoscaler did not add additional nodes during initial spike; scaling happened after ~6 minutes into the spike, too late to avoid user timeouts.
- Scheduler logs show repeated allocation shuffles and context preemption events.
- Background batch jobs (account: infra-batch) were scheduled concurrently on subset of nodes, causing intermittent GPU contention (noisy neighbor pattern).

Immediate impact: Customer production traffic experienced increased latency and partial request failures, impacting SLA and user experience.

Requested outcome: Determine root cause, provide immediate mitigation to stop ongoing timeouts, propose durable fixes to autoscale sizing and noisy-tenant protections.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE/Serving runtime. Asking customer for correlation IDs and their replay harness. SLA timer started.

2026-03-10 09:33 - Marco Hernandez (SRE): Noted high p99 and GPU saturation on pool-us-east-09. Opening investigation; grabbing node-level nvtop and nvidia-smi snapshots. Suspect background batch scheduling overlap.

2026-03-10 09:48 - SparkWrite (Customer): Provided sample request ids: rq_1a2b3c ... rq_1a2b7f and their replay script link: https://gitlab.sparkwrite.com/replay/blueprint. Reported manual retry mitigates some failures.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Marco Hernandez (SRE): Rolled temporary mitigation: cordon nodes running infra-batch in the reservation and moved those jobs to a different maintenance pool. Immediate p99 improved from 2.3s to ~520ms but still above baseline. Continuing deeper analysis.

2026-03-11 14:12 - Emily Zhao (Product): Noted autoscaler configuration for this reservation uses target-utilization 78% and max-instances 12. Investigating whether aggressive target caused late scale-up.

2026-03-12 08:01 - Marco Hernandez (SRE): Identified scheduler preemption churn correlated with mixed sequence-length jobs; KV cache pressure causing per-request overheads when context switches occur. Patch queued to reduce cross-job eviction frequency.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor - infra-batch jobs co-located on some GPU nodes caused sustained high kernel utilization and blocked latency-sensitive inference kernels on those GPUs. Evidence: nvidia-smi samples show deep CUDA kernel queues and high compute util on subset of nodes while others idle.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler mis-sized - target-utilization set too high and cooldown too long, delaying scale-up during burst. Evidence: scale events lagged by ~5-7 minutes; metric shows queue-depth rising before new nodes were provisioned.

Hypothesis 3: Scheduler packing mismatch - mixed long and short sequence workloads causing KV cache thrashing and context-switch overhead resulting in elevated p99 for in-flight requests. Evidence: per-request KV cache miss-rate correlated with latency spikes.

Key dashboards: Grafana - Cluster > pool-us-east-09 > GPU util, Queue depth panel; Tracing - distributed traces for rq_1a2b3c showing 1.2s stall in scheduling layer; Prometheus query snapshots retained at: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/995321-snapshot
Node-level artifacts collected: nvprof traces, dmesg outputs showing no OOM, scheduler debug logs, autoscaler event log. Collected and attached to internal case (see related_confluence_pages).
resolution:
Workarounds applied: 1) Immediately cordoned and drained non-critical batch jobs from the affected reservation to remove noisy neighbors; 2) Temporarily lowered autoscaler target-utilization from 78% to 65% and shortened cooldown to 120s for the reservation to improve scale responsiveness; 3) Enabled strict pod-affinity rules to reduce cross-tenant packing of latency-sensitive jobs with batch jobs.

Fix plan: Short-term - deploy autoscaler config changes cluster-wide for dedicated reservations with mixed workloads and add a scheduling policy flag for 'latency_sensitive' routes to prefer isolated nodes. Medium-term - implement admission controls to prevent batch work from landing on latency-reserved GPUs and add autoscaler predictive scaling based on queue-growth forecasts. Long-term - implement per-reservation kernel isolation heuristics and KV cache residency steering to reduce eviction thrash.

Follow-up actions: Schedule postmortem with customer (SparkWrite) and infra teams; validate changes in staging and monitor p99 over next 72 hours; update dedicated autoscale runbook with new thresholds and noisy-neighbor mitigation checklist.

Status: Mitigations applied and currently observing reduced p99 (baseline ~260ms, current p99 ~480ms during comparable load). Remaining work assigned to SRE (Marco Hernandez) and Scheduler team (Emily Zhao) for permanent fixes. Expected resolution target: 2026-03-18.
